desc: Formalize the model: binary variables h[i][j] (horizontal edge between (i,j) and (i,j+1 mod W)) and v[i][j] (vertical edge between (i,j) and (i+1 mod H,j)); cell validity = allowed port masks (A: turns {NE,ES,SW,WN}; B: straights {NS,EW}).

Derive closed-form characterization: all constraints are linear over GF(2) — A-cell ⟺ h_left⊕h_right=1 ∧ v_top⊕v_bottom=1; B-cell ⟺ h_left⊕h_right=0 ∧ v_top⊕v_bottom=0 ∧ h_left⊕v_top=1 (the third equation excludes empty/crossing). System of 2-variable XOR equations → solvable by weighted DSU; answer = 0 or 2^(#components).
Discard transfer-matrix DP path: unnecessary since the GF(2)/DSU solution is near-linear and handles H,W up to ~1000 and HW ≤ 1e6.

Implement the DSU-with-parity solution with fast I/O; per test case: 2HW variables, equations emitted per cell without storing; iterative find with path compression; track component count and consistency; answer = pow(2, components, 998244353) or 0.

Validate: brute-force enumerator over 4^a·2^b placements for tiny grids; cross-checked DSU solution on exhaustive small boards (2x2, 2x3, 3x3) and random boards up to 4x5, plus the three provided samples (2, 0, 2); stress-tested performance on ~1000x1000 grid and large T.
Finalize: edge cases confirmed (H=2 or W=2 wrap-around with distinct parallel edges, inconsistent → 0); final code reads stdin and writes stdout within required delimiters.
